title: Derived sections–Hom comparison for the point extension model
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $(R,B)$ be either $(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n,(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_s)$ or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$, using the constant and completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].
For an $R$-module $M$ write $\underline M$ for its constant sheaf and put $L_RM=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes, with the explicit adjunction $L_R\dashv\Gamma(s,-)$ sending $h:L_RM\to V$ to $m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m)$, with inverse $t\mapsto(b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U)$ on objects $U$. Assume that $L_R$ and the sections functor $\Gamma(s,-)$ [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] are exact and that $\Gamma(s,B)=R$ through the constant-value map. Let $c$ be any $R$-module complex, represented by a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], and let $B\to I$ be a K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $\Gamma(s,I)$ is K-injective as an $R$-complex, $R\to\Gamma(s,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $L_Rc$ is K-flat as a $B$-complex. There is a natural isomorphism of complexes
$$q_{c,I}:\Gamma\bigl(s,\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_Rc,I)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(c,\Gamma(s,I)),\qquad h\mapsto(m\mapsto h(1\otimes m)),$$
where the sheaf and module Hom complexes use [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-hom-complex] (the module version is the one-object ringed site). It induces $\Gamma(s,R\mathcal Hom_B(L_Rc,B))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$ in the derived category. Under $q_{c,I}$ and the canonical sections–tensor balancing map, the sheaf derived evaluation agrees with module derived evaluation. With factors ordered as $c\otimes\operatorname{Hom}$, both evaluations of homogeneous $h$ of degree $j$ on $x\in c^p$ have value $(-1)^{pj}h(1\otimes x)$. These assertions concern ordinary derived tensor; the integral completed comparison is separate.

source.place: Second sentence: Hom-complex sections comparison on K-flat/K-injective representatives, including evaluation and differential

proof.text: View ordinary $R$-modules as module sheaves on the one-object site with only the maximal covering sieve. Let $a:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Set}$ have inverse image the constant-sheaf functor: a map from the constant presheaf with value $T$ into a sheaf $F$ is precisely a function $T\to F(s)$, and sheafification gives the same adjunction for constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The constant-presheaf functor preserves finite limits objectwise; sheafification preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Thus this is a geometric morphism. With ring map $\underline R\to B$, its module pullback is exactly $L_R$, by the displayed tensor construction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the given K-flat complex $c$ with flat terms: $L_Rc$ is K-flat over $B$ (indeed has flat terms). This uses the general ringed-topos assertion, including its flat-term hypothesis, and does not identify the pro-etale topos with sets.

By [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and the sectionwise products in [def-pur-hom-complex], the degree-$j$ sections of $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_Rc,I)$ are $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_B(L_Rc^p,I^{p+j})$. Apply the assumed explicit adjunction separately to each factor. It gives an $R$-linear bijection to $\prod_p\operatorname{Hom}_R(c^p,\Gamma(s,I^{p+j}))$, sending $h^p$ to $x\mapsto h_s^p(1\otimes x)$. Its inverse sends a family $t^p$ to the sheaf maps locally given by $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,t^p(x)|_U$, extended from constant sections by sheafification. These are mutual inverses by the assumed adjunction, with no finiteness requirement on the product or on $c^p$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), definition of the terms; sites-modules.tex Tag 04TT (section-internal-hom)

proof.text:
The degreewise bijections form a chain isomorphism $q_{c,I}$. In fact [def-pur-hom-complex] gives, for $h$ of degree $j$ and $x\in c^p$,
$$q(dh)^p(x)=d_I(h_s^p(1\otimes x))-(-1)^j h_s^{p+1}(1\otimes d_cx)=(d\,q(h))^p(x).$$
Here the differential on $L_Rc$ is $L_R(d_c)$, so it takes $1\otimes x$ to $1\otimes d_cx$. For chain maps $u:c'\to c$ and $v:I\to I'$, direct substitution gives $q_{c',I'}(vhu)=\Gamma(v)q_{c,I}(h)u$ (with $L_Ru$ on the sheaf side). This proves naturality, including naturality of the inverse.

The exact additive functor $L_R$ is left adjoint to $\Gamma(s,-)$ by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B)$, $\mathcal B=R\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$, $v=L_R$, $u=\Gamma(s,-)$. Since $I$ is K-injective, $\Gamma(s,I)$ is K-injective. Both exactness and the adjunction used here are hypotheses of this item; no injectivity assertion for arbitrary sections functors is being used.

The resolution map $B\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By exactness of sections, in the precise complex form stated in [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], $\Gamma(s,B)\to\Gamma(s,I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Composing it with the assumed constant-value identification $R\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,B)$ gives the specified quasi-isomorphism $R\to\Gamma(s,I)$. Thus the previous step supplies a K-injective resolution of the module complex $R[0]$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), together with the item hypothesis that sections are exact

proof.text: By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the sheaf complex $H=\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(L_Rc,I)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(L_Rc,B)$, and the same definition on the one-object ringed site says that $\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(c,\Gamma(s,I))$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(c,R)$. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], termwise sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so $\Gamma(s,H)$ represents the sections of the former derived object. The chain isomorphism of steps 2--3 therefore gives the asserted derived isomorphism. Independence of the representatives follows from [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] on each of the two ringed sites, and preservation of the resulting quasi-isomorphisms by sections. The naturality already proved on complexes consequently gives naturality of this comparison in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom), construction using K-injective targets; Tag 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined)

proof.text: Use the ordinary derived tensor and the closed structure of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Since $L_Rc$ is K-flat, $L_Rc\otimes_B H$ represents the sheaf derived evaluation's source; since $c$ is K-flat, $c\otimes_R\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(c,\Gamma(s,I))$ represents its module counterpart. The evaluation with Hom first is the counit: on complexes it takes $h\otimes y$ to $h(y)$, as follows by uncurrying the identity of the Hom complex. Reordering to put the argument first uses the specified symmetry of that cited node, and so gives $e(y\otimes h)=(-1)^{pj}h^p(y)$ for $|y|=p$, $|h|=j$. This formula is a chain map: using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and [def-pur-hom-complex], the two $h(dy)$ terms in $e(dy\otimes h+(-1)^p y\otimes dh)$ have coefficients $(-1)^{pj+j}$ and $-(-1)^{pj+j}$, while the remaining term is $(-1)^{pj}d_Ih(y)=d_Ie(y\otimes h)$. This also checks the sign for the ordinary module version.

source.place: Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom and its counit; Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes)

proof.text:
The balancing map needed here is the chain map
$$\beta:c\otimes_R\Gamma(s,H)\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,L_Rc\otimes_B H),\qquad x\otimes h\longmapsto(1\otimes x)\otimes h.$$
It is induced by the unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and by tensoring sections; balancing and restriction follow from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On direct-sum total tensors [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] it is defined on each summand, so no commutation of sections with infinite coproducts is assumed. Its chain-map identity follows from $d(1\otimes x)=1\otimes dx$ and the identical tensor signs on both sides. By step 7,
$$\Gamma(e)\beta(x\otimes h)=(-1)^{pj}h_s^p(1\otimes x)=e_R(x\otimes q_{c,I}(h)).$$
Pure tensors generate each summand of the module tensor, hence the two chain maps are equal. Passing to the derived category proves compatibility of the specified derived evaluations under $q_{c,I}$ and this balancing map. The target is $\Gamma(s,I)\simeq R$ from step 5. This computation uses ordinary tensor throughout and makes no assertion about derived completion.
